correctness.rationale: Properness confines each color class to one part. Any vertex in another nonempty part sees the entire class, forcing its size odd; conversely odd class sizes make every visible neighborhood multiplicity odd. The minimum follows from the minimum number of positive odd summands of each part size. The all-palette count follows by allocating disjoint color sets to parts and using \(A(n,k)=n![z^n](\sinh z)^k\). The optimal-count corollary is algebraically consistent and independently brute-forced on small graphs.
risks: The finite checker is not an infinite proof; correctness of the general theorem relies on the displayed structural argument.

value.rationale: The result gives a natural complete classification and complete coloring enumerator for a canonical dense graph class under a recent invariant. It sharpens the literature’s uniform biclique bound into an exact parity law, extends it to every complete multipartite graph, and distinguishes strong odd coloring sharply from the nearby ordinary odd invariant; the optimal-coloring count adds structural information beyond the minimum number.
risks: The core characterization is short once the correct multipartite viewpoint is recognized; value rests on the completeness, canonical family, exact all-q count, and sharp separation from known bounds rather than proof length.
